                                  15                   Defendant.

                                  17          On July 16, 2026, Defendant removed this case from the Santa Clara County
                                  18   Superior Court based on diversity jurisdiction. ECF 1 at 2. The Complaint alleges
                                  19   Defendant violated the Song-Beverly Consumer Warranty Act by selling Plaintiff a
                                  20   defective 2024 Harley-Davidson motorcycle. Id. For the reasons stated below, the Court
                                  21   ORDERS Defendant to show cause why this case should not be remanded back to state
                                  22   court for failure to satisfy the amount in controversy requirement.
                                  23          Federal courts are courts of limited jurisdiction. Kokkonen v. Guardian Life Ins.
                                  24   Co. of Am., 511 U.S. 375, 377 (1994). District courts have subject matter jurisdiction
                                  25   through federal question or diversity jurisdiction. 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331, 1332. Diversity
                                  26   jurisdiction requires complete diversity of citizenship and an amount in controversy greater
                                  27   than $75,000. 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a). The removing party has the burden of establishing
                                  28   that removal is proper. Lindley Contours LLC v. AAAB Fitness Holdings, Inc., 414 F.
                                          Case 5:26-cv-07313-PCP           Document 6       Filed 07/20/26   Page 2 of 2




                                   1   App’x 62, 64 (9th Cir. 2011).
                                   2          Defendant alleges that this Court has diversity jurisdiction. ECF 1 at 2. Defendant
                                   3   must provide sufficient evidence to show by a preponderance of evidence that the amount
                                   4   in controversy exceeds $75,000. See Urbino v. Orkin Servs. of Cal., Inc., 726 F.3d 1118,
                                   5   1121–22 (9th Cir. 2013) (stating that when a state-court complaint does not clearly plead
                                   6   the minimum amount in controversy, the “removing defendant bears the burden of
                                   7   establishing, by a preponderance of evidence, that the amount in controversy exceeds the
                                   8   jurisdictional threshold”). Defendant contends the amount in controversy is met because
                                   9   Plaintiff seeks actual damages of $15,813.10, a civil penalty of $31,626.20, plus attorney’s
                                  10   fees of $30,000. ECF 1 at 3–6. However, the Court finds $30,000 in attorney’s fees for a
                                  11   straightforward Song-Beverly case to be overly inflated and unlikely, and Defendant
                                  12   provides no basis for this conclusory statement. See Matheson v. Progressive Specialty
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   Ins. Co., 319 F.3d 1089, 1090 (9th Cir. 2003) (“Conclusory allegations as to the amount in
                                  14   controversy are insufficient.”).
                                  15          Accordingly, the Court orders Defendant to, by August 3, 2026, show cause in
                                  16   writing why this case should not be remanded for failure to satisfy the amount in
                                  17   controversy requirement. Plaintiff may respond by August 17, 2026.
                                  18
                                  19          IT IS SO ORDERED.
                                  20
                                  21   Dated: July 20, 2026                       _____________________________________
                                                                                        NATHANAEL M. COUSINS

ORDER REASSIGNING CASE IT IS ORDERED that this case is reassigned using a proportionate, random and blind system pursuant to General Order No. 44 to Magistrate Judge Nathanael M. Cousins. Magistrate Judge Kandis A. Westmore no longer assigned to the case. Counsel are instructed that all future filings shall bear the updated judicial initials immediately after the case number. Counsel are reminded to verify the location of the judge on the court website. All hearing and trial dates presently scheduled are vacated. However, existing briefing schedules for motions remain unchanged. Motions must be renoticed for hearing before the judge to whom the case has been reassigned, but the renoticing of the hearing does not affect the prior briefing schedule. Other deadlines such as those for ADR compliance and discovery cutoff also remain unchanged. Mark B. Busby Clerk, United States District Court (This is a text-only entry generated by the court. There is no document associated with this entry.) (chh, COURT STAFF) (Filed on 7/16/2026) (Entered: 07/16/2026)

Case assigned to Magistrate Judge Kandis A. Westmore. Counsel for plaintiff or the removing party is responsible for serving the Complaint or Notice of Removal, Summons and the assigned judge's standing orders and all other new case documents upon the opposing parties.
